exercises.prompt: On Rand’s statement, to exist is to what?

feedback.quote: To exist is to be something, as distinguished from the nothing of nonexistence, it is to be an entity of a specific nature made of specific attributes.
feedback.note: Existence and identity are not two layers, a bare “that” plus a later “what.”
feedback.citation: Ayn Rand, Galt's Speech, For the New Intellectual, 124

choices.text: Be something, of a specific nature
Be anything one wishes
Be a formless void
Be only a thought

feedback.quote: A is A. A thing is itself.
feedback.note: The second sentence is her plain restatement of the same formula.
feedback.citation: Ayn Rand, Galt's Speech, For the New Intellectual, 125

exercises.prompt: What does “A is A” state about anything that exists?

feedback.quote: A is A. A thing is itself.
feedback.note: Identity is not a label added later. To be is already to be this thing and not some other.
feedback.citation: Ayn Rand, Galt's Speech, For the New Intellectual, 125

choices.text: A thing is itself
A thing is whatever a speaker calls it
A thing is also its opposite, in the same respect
A thing exists without being anything

exercises.prompt: Which situation does she use to state the law of identity?

feedback.quote: A leaf cannot be a stone at the same time, it cannot be all red and all green at the same time, it cannot freeze and burn at the same time.
feedback.note: The law rules out being and not-being in the same respect at the same time. Change across time is a different fact. She discusses change elsewhere. This question uses only the leaf sentence.
feedback.citation: Ayn Rand, Galt's Speech, For the New Intellectual, 125

choices.text: A leaf cannot be a stone at the same time
A leaf cannot change color over a season
A leaf cannot be green on one side
There cannot be two leaves

exercises.prompt: Match the line to the role she gives it.

feedback.quote: You cannot have your cake and eat it, too.
feedback.note: In Galt’s speech that sentence is the simpler statement of identity. Do not confuse it with the one-foot line for epistemology in the 1962 essay, which reverses the word order: eat your cake and have it. Both wordings are quoted in the sources list.
feedback.citation: Ayn Rand, Galt's Speech, For the New Intellectual, 125

pairs.right: Her completion of A is A

pairs.left: You cannot have your cake and eat it, too
pairs.right: Her simpler wording in Galt’s speech

exercises.prompt: “Existence is Identity” means which of these?

feedback.quote: Existence is Identity, Consciousness is Identification.
feedback.note: The second half names consciousness as the act of identifying, not as the maker of identity.
feedback.citation: Ayn Rand, Galt's Speech, For the New Intellectual, 124

choices.text: To be is to be something specific
Existence is a feeling about identity
Identity is invented by language, and existence is not
Only minds have identity

exercises.prompt: Build the completion of the formula.

feedback.quote: Existence is Identity, Consciousness is Identification.
feedback.note: This floor stops at the first half. Consciousness is the next floor.
feedback.citation: Ayn Rand, Galt's Speech, For the New Intellectual, 124

exercises.prompt: When your thinking arrives at a contradiction, where is the error?

feedback.quote: To arrive at a contradiction is to confess an error in one's thinking; to maintain a contradiction is to abdicate one's mind and to evict oneself from the realm of reality.
feedback.note: The error the sentence names is in one’s thinking. Maintaining it, she says in the same breath, throws you out of reality. Reality is not what contains the break.
feedback.citation: Ayn Rand, Galt's Speech, For the New Intellectual, 125

choices.text: Reality contains no contradictions. A contradiction is an error in thinking.
Contradictions are real features of nature
Logic is a game unrelated to facts
Some entities both are and are not, in the same respect

exercises.prompt: In Introduction to Objectivist Epistemology, identity is described as what?

feedback.quote: The first and primary axiomatic concepts are "existence," "identity" (which is a corollary of "existence") and "consciousness."
feedback.note: A corollary here means a restatement of the same primary fact, not a later discovery.
feedback.citation: Ayn Rand, "Axiomatic Concepts," Introduction to Objectivist Epistemology, 55

choices.text: A corollary of existence
A separate universe
An optional assumption
A political slogan

exercises.prompt: For one cake, what does the law of identity rule out?

feedback.quote: You cannot have your cake and eat it, too.
feedback.note: Having the cake and having eaten it cannot both be true of the same cake at once. The clash is in the claim, not in the cake.
feedback.citation: Ayn Rand, Galt's Speech, For the New Intellectual, 125

choices.text: That you still have it and have already eaten it
That you might eat it at a later time
That two people can see the same cake
That a cake is something of a specific nature
